source.title: Extracting SAE task features for in-context learning

record.file_problem: The post text is present, but referenced charts are not included; their numerical values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SAE features can represent and recover task-related information in LLMs, and reports limits to faithful task-vector reconstruction. It also cautions against treating the resulting features as canonical or fully faithful units.
record.gate_note: The post reports results on SAE reconstructions, cleaned task vectors, and feature steering. Chart-based results are described in prose, but the charts and their numerical values are absent. Statements about top features and task-related interpretations are included only where they accompany a reported performance or reconstruction result.
record.test_reason: SAEs are used as a tool on ICL task vectors in Phi-3 Mini and Gemma 2B. Two kinds of result bear on the claim. Direct SAE reconstructions of task vectors lose much or all of their function, which bears on V5 completeness. Single SAE features, used as steering directions, causally drive specific tasks, which bears on V4. The cleanup results compare the authors' own method against task vectors.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also frame the poor direct reconstruction as a consequence of task vectors being off-distribution for SAEs. The low-faithfulness caveat refers to the cleanup method treated as fine-tuning, not to SAE features generally.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies SAE decomposition, loss-guided task-vector cleanup, and steering with task features; it does not apply or reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by task and extraction/insertion layer. Cleanup can make task vectors work at earlier layers; single-feature steering effects depend on the feature/task pairing.
record.problems: Referenced charts are missing, preventing extraction of their numerical results. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Interpretability of features is partly judged by the authors, and the post itself notes low faithfulness to the original behavior and a possible interpretability illusion.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported quantitative outcomes were omitted. Several chart summaries are recorded as aggregate rows because the text gives only aggregate descriptions and the charts are absent.

untested.parts: All of it: toy models, the sparsity transition, and geometry.
All of it: the capacity competition account.
Whether features are distributed across neurons. Only task-related features in two models were examined.
Stability and canonicity across SAEs or seeds. Only reconstruction completeness for off-distribution task vectors was tested.

missing.what: Reconstruction degradation is reported to generalize: "Similar results can be seen in all of the other tasks" (Phi-3)
missing.locator: Initial Phi-3 experiments, Direct SAE task vector reconstruction

missing.what: Dense features persist in cleaned vectors, and removing them significantly hurts performance. Task features in raw reconstructions were buried among dense or repeated-pattern features (top ~30 dense).
missing.locator: Task-related SAE features; Task vector SAE cleanup

missing.what: Comparison with ITO gradient pursuit (target L0 40) reconstruction, shown only in charts

record.verdict_notes: Blog post (Alignment Forum / MATS); charts are absent, so no numeric values exist except the 18.125 vs 14.68 NLL comparison (r4, a method comparison). Feature interpretability is judged by the authors. The V5 challenge is tempered by the off-distribution nature of averaged task vectors.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry of overlapping directions.
Whether polysemanticity results from competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
The study tests SAE-recoverable task features in selected tasks and models, not whether general-purpose features are broadly distributed across neurons in LLMs.
It tests task-vector reconstruction and feature-based task effects, but does not systematically test feature stability across SAEs, training runs, or other representational settings.
No comparison of one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.
